1.a: Entities: Artist, Album, Song, Genre. Artist represents musician/band. Album is collection of songs. Song is individual track. Genre is music category.
1.b: Artist(artist_id PK, name, country). Album(album_id PK, title, release_year, artist_id FK). Song(song_id PK, title, duration, album_id FK, genre_id FK). Genre(genre_id PK, genre_name).
1.c: Yes. Recursive relationship exists: Artist can collaborate with other Artist. Implemented via separate table Collaborations(artist1_id FK, artist2_id FK).

2.a: Primary key is A (or E). Closure of {A}+ = A,B,C,D,E. A->BC, B->D gives D, CD->E gives E. Also E->A so E is candidate key.
2.b: Insertion anomaly: cannot insert employee without department. Deletion anomaly: deleting last student removes course info. Update anomaly: changing professor name needs multiple row updates.
2.c: 3NF decomposition: R1(A,B,C) with FD A->BC. R2(B,D) with FD B->D. R3(C,D,E) with FD CD->E. R4(E,A) with FD E->A. All FDs preserved, all relations in 3NF.

3.a: Atomicity: transaction completes fully or aborts. Consistency: DB constraints preserved. Isolation: concurrent execution appears serial. Durability: committed changes persist after crash.
3.b: Schedule S1: R1(A),W1(A),R2(A),W2(A),R2(B),W2(B),R1(B),W1(B) → not conflict serializable (cycle T1->T2 on A, T2->T1 on B). Schedule S2: R1(A),R2(A),R1(B),R2(B),W1(A),W2(B) → conflict serializable (equivalent to T1 then T2).
3.c: 2PL applied: T1: lock-X(A), read(A), lock-S(B), read(B), write(A), unlock(A), unlock(B). T2: lock-S(B), read(B), lock-X(A) → blocked until T1 releases A. No deadlock. Strict 2PL prevents cascading aborts.

4.a: Query1 (students in DBMS): π name (Student ⋈ (σ title='DBMS' Course ⋈ Enroll)). Query2 (students took all courses): π sid (Enroll ÷ π cid (Course)). Query3 (courses with no students): π cid (Course) - π cid (Enroll).
4.b: Tuple calculus Q1: {s.name | Student(s) ∧ ∃e∈Enroll ∃c∈Course (e.sid=s.sid ∧ e.cid=c.cid ∧ c.title='DBMS')}. Q2: {s.name | Student(s) ∧ ∀c∈Course (∃e∈Enroll (e.sid=s.sid ∧ e.cid=c.cid))}. Q3: {c.title | Course(c) ∧ ¬∃e∈Enroll (e.cid=c.cid)}.

5.a: Blocking factor = floor(4096/200) = 20 records/block. Total blocks = ceil(10000/20) = 500 blocks. Index blocking factor = floor(4096/(4+6)) = floor(4096/10) = 409 index entries per block (assuming 4-byte key).
5.b: NoSQL types: Key-Value (Redis), Document (MongoDB), Column-family (Cassandra), Graph (Neo4j). Mapping from relational: Table → Collection (Document) or Column Family; Row → Document; Join → Embedded document or graph edge; Foreign key → Reference.
